newsitem.title: TANZANIA: U.N. agency helps 200,000 Tanzanian drought victims.
newsitem.headline: U.N. agency helps 200,000 Tanzanian drought victims.

text.p: The U.N. World Food Programme is pressing ahead with emergency relief for 200,000 Tanzanian drought victims including families suffering near-starvation, WFP country director Irene Lacy said on Wednesday.
She told Reuters that a further 400,000 drought victims were being given emergency food aid by the Tanzanian government.
Recent contributions worth $4 million received from Australia, Canada, Belgium, Ireland and Germany had allowed relief to extend into a seventh week.
"The support we received from these donors is very, very important to help us avoid a far more serious problem," Lacy said.

She said WFP teams had reported that some Tanzanian families were eating only one meal a day of less than 1,300 calories. As a comparison, a refugee diet is deemed inadequate if it falls below 1,900 calories, Lacy said.
Worst-affected areas included northern Arusha, Kilimanjaro and Tanga regions, central Dodoma and southern Lindi, government officials said.
Lacy said Western donor funds were used to cover food procurement, transport, distribution and monitoring.
She said the food relief would go on until July or September, after which locally harvested grains should start coming onto the market.
Tanzania's poor network of secondary roads was adding to problems of getting food to the worst areas.
"Distribution is a bit of a nightmare in some regions," Lacy said, adding that roads were so bad in southern Lindi that boats were used to deliver food.
According to latest WFP figures, drought was likely to result in a cereal shortfall in Tanzania of 500,000 tonnes this year compared to normal annual production of 6.7 million tonnes.
